quienes.p1: We are a wildlife rescue center and a sanctuary for animals rescued from the illegal species trade, from accidents caused by humans, and from abuse victims.
quienes.p2: We have a fully equipped veterinary clinic to receive animals in danger, with serious injuries or at risk of death.
quienes.p3: We also have a sanctuary where animals that could not be returned to the wild live, either because they were taken from their natural habitat just weeks after birth, because they require ongoing veterinary care, or because their injuries no longer allow them to survive in the wild.
quienes.p4: At the rescue you will find species such as the two-toed sloth
quienes.p4b: being one of the most rescued species due to illegal trafficking and accidents on power lines.
quienes.p5a: You will also meet the white-faced capuchin monkey
quienes.p6a: A diversity of birds such as the scarlet macaw
quienes.historiaP1: In 2009, the rescue center was founded on the Caribbean coast of Costa Rica, in Moín. Its first rescue was Buda, an animal saved from the illegal wildlife trade just before being sold as a pet.
quienes.historiaP2: The center, located in Moín, also patrolled the beaches to protect the nests of an endangered species: the leatherback sea turtle
quienes.historiaP3: However, illegal egg collectors were not the only challenge. The construction of a major port in Moín threatened the rescue and conservation activities. As an act of intimidation, environmental activist Jairo Mora Sandoval was murdered while defending the sea turtle nests.
quienes.historiaP4: Due to growing pressure and the loss of access to the original property, the center was forced to relocate to San Miguel de Turrúcares. There, a temporary property was generously lent so the animals could be housed while a permanent solution was sought.
quienes.historiaP5: The original property in Moín was occupied and, in 2016, after selling two personal properties, the rescue center's owner was able to acquire the land where the center now operates, a property that is still being paid for, which is why we look for volunteers like you to be part of the care and protection of our wildlife.

volunteers.title: Volunteering
volunteers.imgAlt: Volunteers at the Costa Rica Animal Rescue Center
volunteers.p1: Our volunteers are people who have decided to donate an important part of their time and dedication to our cause, which is why we have created a safe, fun space that ensures coexistence and cultural exchange.
volunteers.p2: All our programs include meals and lodging. We have the necessary infrastructure for you to choose what is best for your well-being and comfort, which also guarantees you have space to practice the activities you enjoy most, such as yoga, reading, and exploring nature. What else can you imagine doing?
volunteers.p3: The experience includes getting to know the town and the chance to take part in the activities we have planned for you while we wait for you: bonfires, karaoke, tours and much more.

hospital.title: Hospital
hospital.p1: To rehabilitate wildlife, our volunteers are crucial. They heal wounds, handle hospital emergencies, take care of the demanding feeding of baby animals, and participate in surgeries and other medical interventions.
hospital.p2: Our main purpose is to rehabilitate species, many of them endangered, and return them to the wild — that is where our true purpose lies.
hospital.p3: If you are a veterinary medicine or nursing student, or you are discovering your calling, this is the ideal place for you.

habitacion.compartidaHighlight: Share a room with people of similar interests and make connections.
habitacion.compartidaDesc: Enjoy shared lodging with three meals a day, daily room cleaning and unforgettable activities.
habitacion.privadaHighlight: Keep your privacy in a room with a private bathroom.
habitacion.privadaDesc: Enjoy private lodging with three meals a day, daily room cleaning and unforgettable activities.
habitacion.familiarDesc: Enjoy accommodation in the village; we take care of round-trip transportation to the rescue center.

visitanos.title: Visit us
visitanos.p1: Come see the sanctuary and the rescued animals that are permanent residents of the center. You can come with the whole family; our opening hours are Monday to Sunday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm.
visitanos.p2: We are located in Cebadilla de Turrúcares, in the province of Alajuela. The tour lasts about an hour and you will always have a trained guide at the rescue.

giras.title: Educational tours
giras.p1: Tours designed for schools, colleges and groups. Learn about wildlife conservation and the work of the rescue center.
giras.p2: An experience that combines environmental education, contact with nature and moments that last forever.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: We are open every day from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, including holidays.
faq.q2: How do we get to the center?
faq.a2: Search for Costa Rica Animal Rescue Center, in Cebadilla de Turrúcares.
faq.q3: How much is the entrance fee?
faq.a3: Nationals: adults ₡6000, children ₡4000. Foreigners: adults $20, children $10.
faq.a4: Yes, we have guided tours designed for families and school groups.
